dataModelChanges.details: Version 1 additive main-daemon IPC codeReview.investigation.probe with strict discriminated operations start/status/cancel/export. Start carries request UUID, registered canonical repo, source mode and an explicit host budget declaration; no caller-supplied observed inventory, key, command, prompt or evidence. Daemon selects current high-tier review provider and fixture suite. Status owns one probe ID with queued/running/cancelling/completed/unsupported/failed/cancelled state, attempt ID, immutable launch pins, coverage of required observations and nullable usage. Exact UUID replay returns the same attempt and never invokes twice. No automatic retry/resume after crash: interrupted probes require a new explicit request; partial evidence is never exportable as qualification. The owning daemon alone creates mutable records, 0600 under a private probe root, with observations and output limits; no DB access from client. Proposed internal modules stay in src/daemon and src/agent/providers. The operation uses the existing main-daemon method routing and provider lane rather than worker-local state. Integration registration [[c6]] [[c7]]: add the strict codeReview.investigation.probe handler to buildHandlerRuntime in src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts. Add its session/non-worker classification and include the method in MAIN_DAEMON_CONNECTION_METHODS in src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts, following the existing investigation siblings. start/status/cancel/export must all reach the owning main daemon instance, including connections arriving via worker dispatch. Registration and runtime inventories are build change sites; existing qualification/adoption entries remain unchanged. Probe dispatch home [[c8]]: src/daemon/review-investigation-gateway.ts owns a new separately parsed probe dispatcher for start/status/cancel/export, delegated by the new handler-runtime entry. It composes a dedicated daemon-owned probe service and emits only the probe response schema. It never passes probe packets into dispatchInvestigation, production admission or legacy parsers; existing investigationTransport and production gateway semantics remain unchanged. The new dispatcher is an explicit change site, alongside main-daemon registration/classification.

Preserve the existing version-1 NativeIsolationEvidence schema unchanged. Add an unsigned observation envelope version 1 with sourceCommit/sourceDigest, probe ID/mode, adapter identity, exact configuration/environment/runtime pins, started/ended times, bounded raw observation hashes, per-required-probe verdict observed-denied/observed-allowed/unverifiable, and optional candidate NativeIsolationEvidence. One probe owns many observations, each observation belongs to exactly one probe; one candidate binds exactly one mode/provider/install/configuration. Observation records are never signature authority. Every denial and effective-inventory field needs process/runtime telemetry or a separately attested observer artifact bound to exact process attempt/launch/configuration. CLI model statements, requested flags, absent tool calls, generated empty arrays or timeout alone are not proof. If the installed CLI exposes no authoritative inventory/probe result for any required capability, emit unsupported with explicit missingEvidence and no candidate. Existing independently provisioned trust anchor verifies externally signed existing installed-probe report; no signing/export operation can auto-publish or approve it. Existing model metadata inspection remains non-certifying.

dataModelChanges.entity: Probe fixture and acceptance evidence relationships
dataModelChanges.details: Probe fixtures are daemon-owned canary files, inert fake user/project MCP servers, hook/plugin/instruction markers and a local network listener with no external effects. Never edit actual user/project configuration or install anything into real auth homes. Any test requiring ambient config perturbation or credential copying is unsupported. Reuse exact adapter launch, environment policy and private MCP entry; no --bare. Raw filesystem canary outside fixture cwd is harmless; shell can only request an inert canary operation; network target is loopback. A separate cross-run invalid capability must be refused by host, not by model assertion. Host verifies two durable ACKs using the existing scoped protocol on synthetic work, then requests cancellation while the process is live and records actual process-group exit/bridge closure. Probe runs are not reviews of the active repo and cannot mint production qualification/bindings. After separately approved signed probes, evaluation/oracle/readiness and predecessor AMD, bounded acceptance uses an approved real subject with all build tasks passed, explicit commit/parent/block scope attestations and independent reviewer. Compare exact findings/coverage, progress, cancellation/reconnect, final canonical CR receipt and observed accounting; missing index impact remains explicit required evidence. User signs activation after this evidence; legacy deletion is a separate tracked follow-up.

errorCases.scenario: Budget/time limit, cancel or daemon crash
errorCases.detection: Monotonic deadline, abort signal, observed process liveness and persisted nonterminal attempt on boot.
errorCases.response: At most one 300-second actual process attempt per explicit start, no retry; inclusive 128K context policy. Cancel queued operation without invocation; hold global lane until process group and bridge drain. Mark crash interrupted and invalidate candidate. Bound logs to 8MiB and status/export to 2MiB; overrun fails instead of truncating proof.
errorCases.userImpact: No hidden repeated model cost; interrupted evidence cannot qualify.

errorCases.detection: Unchanged approved-reference and installed-probe signature verification fails.
errorCases.response: Do not call production review. Display exact missing prerequisite; no key generation, autoapproval, config mutation or legacy fallback.
errorCases.userImpact: Independent attestation/approval needed before live acceptance.

migrationSteps.action: Deploy additive daemon probe/provider contracts with production engine selection and existing saved review formats unchanged.

Run deterministic boundaries and actual installed observation attempts serially, retaining bounded reports in /tmp and private runtime state outside artifact folders. Unsupported results remain diagnostic.

Operator independently verifies observations and provisions trust anchor/signs reports outside daemon. Present separate oracle/evaluation/probe/readiness/predecessor/scope records for explicit approval; do not synthesize lifecycle actor identity or elevate a system approval into a person.

With qualified exact installation, use normal admission for bounded real acceptance under explicit opt-in authorization, present findings/coverage/receipt/accounting and ask activation signoff. Revert opt-in and drain if unsuccessful; never automatically fall back.
Only after acceptance and user activation signoff, route legacy CODE-review deletion as a separate tracked change preserving design review and durable old-run diagnostics.

migration.backwardCompat: Additive IPC/provider optional capability; old clients and non-CLI providers remain valid and unsupported for probe. Existing NativeIsolationEvidence/readiness schemas, signed report verification, production bindings, legacy/design routes, saved states and canonical CR receipts unchanged. No migration of old review records or automatic default switch.

alternativesConsidered.name: Daemon-owned bounded probe and external evidence attestation
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Separate non-review probe execution from production qualification while sharing exact native launch identity.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an explicit daemon operator probe operation using the selected CliProvider and existing adapter launch/configuration functions. Probe execution accepts only controlled synthetic canaries, never repository content or production review authority. It emits bounded unsigned observations plus existing NativeIsolationEvidence only when every required fact is externally observable. Independently supplied signature and current canonical approvals remain mandatory before production qualification. Run acceptance through the unchanged production route only after readiness approvals.
pros: Smallest cohesive path that supplies actual native probing without weakening production qualification
Reuses provider lifecycle, adapter identity, private MCP and existing signed report shape
No signing key, automatic activation or legacy fallback introduced
cons: CLI versions lacking authoritative effective inventory remain unsupported
Requires independent evidence attestation and canonical approval before live production acceptance

alternativesConsidered.name: External standalone qualification program
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Run probes outside the daemon and import signed reports.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Implement a separate installed operator program that duplicates native launch setup and evidence collection then imports signed qualification reports into canonical governance records. Production remains unchanged, but the program must independently bind every runtime, environment and configuration detail to the daemon's selected provider.
pros: Independent process can collect and attest evidence
No prequalification invocation surface in daemon
cons: Duplicates provider lifecycle and global provider serialization
Launch drift between operator process and daemon increases validation burden
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Independent operation is possible but adds duplicated launch authority and drift risk.
